claim: Bases is officially defined by Obsidian as a core plugin that lets you create database-like views of your notes, storing data in local Markdown files and their properties.
quote: Bases is a core plugin that lets you create database-like views of your notes. ... All the data in Obsidian Bases is stored in your local Markdown files and their properties.

claim: Obsidian launched Bases as a new core plugin in version 1.9, displaying dynamic views of notes as tables, cards, and lists, with 1.10 adding Bases APIs for custom view layouts.
quote: Recently we launched Obsidian 1.9 with Bases, a new core plugin that lets you display dynamic views of your notes as tables, cards, and now lists. ... Today, we're releasing Obsidian 1.10 beta with Bases APIs to help you create your own custom view layouts.

claim: Obsidian 1.9.0 Desktop became available in early access on May 21, 2025 with Bases as the headline feature for turning note collections into structured databases.
quote: Obsidian 1.9.0 (Desktop) became available in early access on May 21, 2025. The headline feature in the 1.9.0 update is a new core plugin called Bases, which lets you turn collections of notes into structured databases.

claim: The Bases file format and formula syntax were refined in 1.9.2 (June 5, 2025), adding file properties like file.path, file.links, and file.tags and object-oriented chainable functions.
quote: New file properties: `file.path`, `file.links` (a list of all internal links in this file), and `file.tags` ... Functions are now object-oriented. Instead of `contains(file.name, "Books")`, the formula would be `file.name.contains("Books")`.

claim: Unlike Dataview, Bases require no coding — they are created and edited entirely with a visual editor and are fast even on large vaults.
quote: Bases are incredibly powerful. They are fast to create, fast to update, and return results incredibly fast ... Bases don't require any coding. You can create and edit Bases entirely with a visual editor.

claim: A base is conceptually a table of notes selected by filters such as tag or folder, with two sequential filter layers (All views, then This view).
quote: A base has two sections for filters, one titled All views, the second one This view. These are applied sequentially: first the "All views" filter selects a subset of your notes, then the "This view" filter prunes this selection further.

claim: Community framing positions Bases as the biggest Obsidian update since Properties, replacing the role Dataview has played for power users.
quote: Obsidian's New Bases Feature is The Biggest Update Since Properties

claim: Bases is positioned as the official, first-party successor to the Dataview community plugin, which has stagnated.
quote: How to Migrate to Obsidian Bases from Dataview

claim: Three ways to create a new base: command palette ('Bases: Create new base' or 'Bases: Insert new base'), right-click a folder in the file explorer and pick 'New base', or click 'Create new base' in the ribbon.
quote: Bases: Create new base (same folder as active file) or Bases: Insert new base (creates and embeds in current file)... Right-click your desired folder, select New base... Click 'Create new base' in the vertical ribbon menu

claim: A .base YAML file has five top-level sections: filters (global), formulas (computed properties), properties (display config), summaries (aggregations), and views (rendering definitions).
quote: filters — Global conditions applied to all views; formulas — Custom calculated properties; properties — Configuration metadata for properties; summaries — Custom aggregation formulas; views — Data rendering definitions

claim: Bases ships four built-in view layouts: Table and Cards (added in Obsidian 1.9), plus List and Map (added in 1.10); Map requires the Maps plugin.
quote: Table — Display files as rows in a table... Cards — Display files as a grid of cards. Lets you create gallery-like views with images... List — Display files as a list with bulleted or numbered markers... Map — Display files as pins on an interactive map. Requires the Maps plugin.

claim: Cards view configuration includes card width, an image property (accepting [[wiki]] attachments, URLs, or hex colours), and an image fit setting of cover (crop to fill) or contain (scale to fit).
quote: Cover: The image fills the card's content box. If it does not fit, the image will be cropped. Contain: The image is scaled until it fits within the card's content box. The image will not be cropped.

claim: Practical filter workflow: click 'Filters' top-right, pick 'file' from the property dropdown, choose 'has tag', then pick a tag — the base updates instantly to all notes matching that tag.
quote: Click 'Filters' in the top right of your Base... Select 'file' from the Property dropdown... Choose 'has tag' from the filter type menu... the Base will instantly update to show me all of my notes with that tag

claim: A useful starting column set for a first table view is file.name, two or three note properties, and a temporary file.path debugging column you remove once filters are correct.
quote: For your initial table view, start with 3–5 columns: file.name, 2–3 note properties, and one debugging column like file.path (removable later)

claim: A complete community book-library Index.base file is published on GitHub with filters on folder, multiple table and cards views (All Books, Queue, Published, Series Cards, By Year, Current Year), formulas for cover image, rating, series, and reading-years.
quote:
filters:
  and:
    - file.folder.contains("Personal/Reading/Books")
    - file.ext != "base"
formulas:
  Title: link(file.path, title)
  Rating: if(rating == null, "N/A", ["⭐", rating.toString()].join(" "))
  Cover: image(cover)

claim: Practical PKM's book-library recipe uses a folder-path filter on the Book Notes folder with three views: a default table, a primary cards view showing cover/author/rating/pages, and a filtered '5 Star Books' cards view (rating == 5).
quote: Only shows files where the file path begins with Book Notes... Cards View - Primary display with cover images, configured to show author, rating, and page number... 5 Star Books View - Filtered cards showing only books where the rating property is ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

claim: A reading-log recipe demonstrates the readDates pattern using array filtering: a Read-by-Year view applies the filter readDates.toString().contains('2025') and a formula readDates.filter(value.toString().contains('2025')) on book notes that have a shelf and series property.
quote: Read by year filter: Advanced filter using "where readDates.toString().contains('2025')"... Functions applied: image(cover), link(file.name, title), and readDates.filter(value.toString().contains("2025"))

claim: An Obsidian forum 'Share & showcase' template for project/task tracking standardises four frontmatter keys — status, passion (1–5), deadline (datetime), progress (0–100) — and groups columns into source / display (emoji + progress-bar formulas) / sort categories.
quote:
status: In Progress
passion: 5
deadline: 2025-08-19T12:51:00
progress: 60 ... status field includes default options: "To Do, In Progress, Focus, On Hold, Cancelled, Completed"

claim: A 'home base' tutorial provides two complete table-view base configs: a whole-vault Note Checklist (file.inFolder('') and file.ext=='md') and a Projects & Exams base filtering on tags containsAny('projects','exam') with a tags containsAny('task') refinement, plus priOrder + due-date sorting.
quote:
filters:
  and:
    - file.tags.containsAny("projects", "exam")
    - file.tags.containsAny("task")

claim: A meeting-notes recipe builds two bases off a Type=='Meeting' note schema with Attendees and Projects multi-link properties: an Attendee base filtering Type=='Meeting' AND Attendees.contains(this.file), and a Project base using Projects.contains(this.file).
quote: For Attendee Base: The filter condition should be: Type == "Meeting" AND Attendees.contains(this.file). For Project Base: The filter condition should be: Projects.contains(this.file) AND Type == "Meeting"

claim: The Obsidian TV Tracker plugin demonstrates a movie/TV media-log frontmatter shape — title, type, status (Watchlist/Watched/Complete/Incomplete/In Progress), priority, rating, dates, progress, external link — that is directly usable as a Bases source schema.
quote: Each Movie and TV show is saved as a markdown file in a folder of your choice, with each file containing YAML content which is used to display, filter and sort content... For watchlist entries, you should enter 'Watchlist' as the status

claim: A 'Bases of Bases' showcase thread shows a cards-view-with-cover pattern that derives a thumbnail from each base's filename using the formula file.basename + '.jpg', useful as a home/index page across all your bases.
quote: a user created a Base of Bases with a Cards view using a formula property for cover images. The specific detail mentioned is that the "Cover Image" property uses the formula `file.basename + ".jpg"`

claim: A community recipe-database template tags notes with #🍽️/recipe and uses a multi-select ingredients property (curated from ~300 common ingredients via Metadata Menu) so ingredient-overlap queries are possible — directly portable to a Bases filter on ingredients.contains(...).
quote: FROM #🍽️/recipe WHERE ingredients FLATTEN ingredients as ings... utilizing the Metadata Menu plugin to enable multi-select ingredient properties sourced from a curated list of approximately 300 common cooking ingredients

claim: Bases lacks Dataview's GROUP BY equivalent and currently only ships Table and Cards views (List/Kanban planned); it requires YAML frontmatter and cannot read inline key::value, so the Dataview-to-Properties plugin is used to lift inline data into properties first.
quote: Grouping functionality - Currently unavailable in Bases, though grouping options are currently in development. View types - Only two options exist: Table and Cards (List and Kanban views are planned). Bases requires YAML properties in note frontmatter, not inline key-value pairs.

claim: Bases-Toolbox by Quorafind provides a Dataview-to-Bases converter web tool supporting TABLE queries with fields, aliases, FROM, WHERE, SORT, LIMIT and GROUP BY — but not DataviewJS.
quote: Supports most common Dataview features including fields with aliases, FROM sources, WHERE conditions, SORT operations, LIMIT, and GROUP BY. Notably, the documentation makes no mention of DataviewJS support.

claim: On Hacker News, users characterise Bases as roughly a 90% replacement for Dataview that is faster and GUI-driven, and note the Dataview author's own successor Datacore is stalled.
quote: It's not meant to be as 'kitchen sink' comprehensive yet, but it's like 90% replacement and faster ... The author of dataview admitted to that [poor syntax design]. The author started working on a new dataview-like plugin called datacore, but that project is stalled.

claim: Dataview's DQL is brittle, has no GUI, is read-only, and is not supported by Obsidian Publish — limitations Bases addresses directly.
quote: Queries can be brittle, breaking easily with syntax errors ... there is no graphical user interface (GUI) for building Dataview queries ... Dataview queries are not supported by Obsidian Publish ... Dataview could fetch data, but it could not make changes.

claim: Commentators frame Dataview as 'resting peacefully in a long-term academic sabbatical' rather than actively developed, with Bases positioned as the official successor.
quote: Dataview is no longer being actively developed ... not dead, but let's say, resting peacefully in a long-term academic sabbatical.

claim: The Dataview repository still shows ~9,000 stars and shipped version 0.5.70 on April 7 2025 with no README sunset notice, so it is technically maintained but slowly.
quote: Star Count: 9,000 stars. Last Commit Date: April 7, 2025 (version 0.5.70 released). No explicit maintenance mode, frozen, deprecated, or sunset notes appear in the README.

claim: Bases only operates at the note level and does not read inline properties or inline tasks the way Dataview does.
quote: Bases only does note level. I used Dataview to pull all of my checklist items up for each page... Bases doesn't do inline properties, but I never used that.

claim: Bases cannot index individual tasks because task details live in file body, not properties; users want task-level filtering, urgency, Kanban/Gantt views.
quote: The actual task details are in the file contents, which aren't read by bases.

claim: The Bases date() formula fails on ISO8601 timestamps with seconds/offset and on this.file.ctime — only YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM works, contradicting the docs.
quote: ISO8601 timestamps with seconds and offset (e.g., "2025-10-14T20:54:08-03:00") return nothing. The this.file.ctime property also fails with the date conversion.

claim: Bases has no working horizontal scroll for wide tables — neither scrollbar nor Shift+wheel works because the last column expands to fill space.
quote: No horizontal scroll bar appears nor Shift + Mouse Wheel works... the app treats the last column according to its true width not the apparent width, so it appears like it doesn't scroll anymore.

claim: Filter equality on array properties is inconsistent — newly created notes matching a filter fail to appear until manually re-edited; the .contains() syntax is the workaround.
quote: Changing the filter to Note ["Topic-Type"] == "Browser" causes the note to appear, but other matching notes then disappear. Manual workaround required... closing and reopening Obsidian entirely did not resolve the problem.

claim: Bases can stutter badly even on small datasets (50 files, 19 properties); disabling hardware acceleration is a known workaround.
quote: Whenever I try to scroll through my base on my PC it's incredibly slow and stutters... I have about 50 files with about 19 properties. There are four views within the base.

claim: Mobile parity is imperfect: a vault's Bases sync to iOS but render empty rows despite identical data on desktop (reported Apr 2026, iOS 26.5, Obsidian 1.12.7).
quote: The 'Base' table view loads, but no content is displayed. It appears empty, as if a filter is applied that returns no results, even though the table contains data on Desktop.

claim: As of mid-2026, Kanban view is still 'in progress' and Calendar view plus Publish support for Bases remain on the planned (unshipped) roadmap.
quote: Active (In Progress): Kanban view for Bases — Display files in side-by-side kanban boards. Planned: Bases support for Publish; Calendar view for Bases.

claim: Bases scored 4.4/5 community but is flagged 'still a bit of a work in progress' with a steep learning curve, weak documentation, and no Publish integration yet.
quote: The capabilities are great but there needs to be better documentation...it has a steep learning curve and is also missing some key building blocks.

claim: On iPadOS/iOS, creating or duplicating a Bases view through the GUI fails to focus the new view, making it appear to silently fail unless the keyboard is toggled.
quote: the new view isn't automatically focused on, which makes the creation appear to fail unless the onscreen keyboard is opened and then closed.

claim: Embedded Bases have no display-height limit or vertical scrollbar, so an embed in a note can blow out the page layout.
quote: requests to limit the display height and add vertical scroll bars when a base is embedded.

claim: Global functions include if(condition, trueResult, falseResult?), now(), today(), date(), duration(), link(), list(), file(), image(), icon(), max(), min(), number() — covering conditionals, dates, and value coercion.
quote: if() – Conditional logic: "if(condition, trueResult, falseResult?)"; now() – Current datetime; today() returns midnight today; duration() – Parses duration strings for date arithmetic

claim: Bases re-renders reliably when frontmatter is edited through Obsidian's own properties UI, but plugins that write via app.vault.modify() can leave the metadata index stale until the cache is rebuilt (Settings → Files and Links → Rebuild Cache); using app.fileManager.processFrontMatter() avoids the issue.
quote: This plugin automatically updates a frontmatter status in a file. This is being updated within the file, but both Bases AND Dataview are not updating to reflect the change ... after that it will not update again until the cache is rebuilt.
